title: Pipeline Code Walkthrough
subtitle: How our fact-checking instrument turns one claim into one number, end to end, with the real source code embedded. Frozen reading copy for the model-spec and pre-registration write-up.

sections.title: 0. Overview and glossary
sections.prose:
This page is the reading copy of our fact-checking instrument, with the real source code embedded. It is meant to be read top to bottom by someone who has never opened the repo. Every code block is pulled verbatim from the frozen commit by the build script; nothing here is paraphrased.

The instrument turns one short claim into one number. We extract check-worthy claims from a post, write one search query per claim, retrieve the top ten documents, read each (claim, document) pair with an LLM that returns one of a few flags, and add up fitted per-flag log-odds weights into an evidence score. A score below a fitted boundary means we flag the claim as likely false.

One thing to hold on to before you read on. The SHIPPED instrument (frozen 2026-09-21) is read-v5 (seven flags: 5,4,3,X,I,2,1), fit on fc_gold_bal3000 with boundary -4.0115; it is the DEFAULT the main runner uses and the survey pool is scored under. An earlier six-flag experiment, read-v6.1, was the shipped fit on 2026-09-14 to 2026-09-21; it is now archived (headline_metrics_v61_sixflag_2026-09-21.json) and stays selectable via --reader read-v6.1. Section 15 lays out exactly which files and weights belong to which. Where the code and the notes disagree, this page follows the code and flags the disagreement.

glossary.def: our name for the scoring model: each document is a coloured ball (its flag), and the claim's score is the summed log-odds of the balls drawn. The name comes from the Truth Odds framing.

the single label a read assigns to one (claim, document) pair. Seven in read-v5 (5,4,3,X,I,2,1), six in read-v6.1 (the '3' removed). 5=establishes claim, 1=disproves it, X=on-claim context, I=irrelevant.
one LLM call that judges one document against one claim and returns a flag plus the sentence numbers it relied on.
the seven-flag reader prompt (READ_SYS_MODE, hash 92404a300e14). The FROZEN survey-selection reader.

the six-flag reader prompt (READ_SYS_V6_1, hash 57d8dbc5df6d) = read-v5 with the '3' button removed and nothing else. The 2026-09-14 shipped experiment; superseded 2026-09-21 by the read-v5 freeze, still selectable via --reader read-v6.1.

the score threshold below which a claim is flagged as likely false. Chosen as the nested out-of-fold threshold at 2% false-positive rate. -4.0115 (the SHIPPED read-v5 freeze on bal3000); -3.5839 was the archived read-v6.1 rep1500 fit.

the frozen survey weights file weights_v5_ceiling_bal3000.json and its boundary -4.0115; the freeze the survey pool selection uses. Written into headline_metrics.json 2026-09-21 by fit_ceiling_weights.py --ship (see section 15).

the Serper-only production-regime arm (date ceiling off, echo-pass leak control). Its six-flag weights + boundary -6.7949 live in prodregime_metrics.json and were used to score the survey pool on 2026-09-16.
the labelled claim set harvested from fact-checkers, frozen at 3,280 claims (populations/fc_gold.parquet). The training/validation set for the weights.

fc_gold_rep1500.parquet, a 1,500-claim balanced slice (750 true / 750 false, seed 20260914) drawn from the frozen 3,236 that tracks full-corpus difficulty; the fitting population for the shipped six-flag instrument.
a proxy veracity label for a Community Notes post (a currently-helpful 'misinformed' note = quasi-false). A post-level suspicion signal, not a fact-check verdict.
the label-free urn populations: Community Notes false posts, wire-service true posts, and the mixed X feed (feed_mixed is the file x_feed.parquet). Used for the two-urn transfer test.
whether a claim is about who SAID something (attribution) or about the world (assertion). Defined in claim_modes.py; importable but stripped out of the read-v5 production prompt.
out-of-fold area under the ROC curve: AUC computed on held-out folds in 5-fold cluster-disjoint cross-validation, so weights never score their own training claims.
the fraction of truly-false claims we flag while holding false positives on true claims at 2%. The instrument's headline operating point.
every claim's document slots are padded to ten silent (no-direction) slots before summing weights, so a claim with few retrieved documents is not scored as more certain than one with ten.
a short hash of a prompt's text stamped into every run record (eval/prompt_hash.py), so a run can be tied to the exact prompt bytes that produced it.
we never let a claim's own source verify it: the origin publisher's domain (and x.com for a tweet) is excluded from retrieval. Logic in run_claim + verify_tweet_claims helpers.

sections.title: 1. How a run is launched
sections.prose: Every run is a Python module under eval.scripts.build_eval, launched with `uv run python -m ...`. The main retrieval+read runner is `evidence_urn_run` (E1, fc_gold); the Community-Notes survey uses `cn_survey_verify` (verify) + `cn_survey_score` (score). All read model, DeepInfra base URL and API key come from `src/config.py` (VERIFICATION_MODEL = DeepSeek-V4-Flash, EXTRACTION_BASE_URL = DeepInfra OpenAI-compatible endpoint, key from env DEEPINFRA_API_KEY via python-dotenv). The key-claim survey chain (extract -> filter -> screen) runs before evidence_urn_run to select claims. All chain stages default to DeepSeek-V4-Flash on the deepinfra provider.

sections.title: 2b. Dataset lineage: how each reported dataset was built
sections.prose:
Every headline number in this page rests on a small set of frozen datasets. This section traces each one back to the committed code that produced it, so a reader can see exactly how the evaluation populations were built — not just what they contain. The table below maps each reported dataset to its builder script (and the key function), the seed or rule that makes the draw reproducible, and which result it feeds.

Two facts are load-bearing. First, the labelled fc_gold set is pulled fresh from the Google Fact Check Tools API by harvest_full.py; it is NOT built from the per-publisher scrapers (Snopes/PolitiFact/AFP/...), which built a separate legacy eval set and are now archived under src/_archive/factcheck_harvest_lib/. Second, two datasets that back reported numbers have NO committed builder — they are pinned files with no script in the repo that writes them; they are flagged in the table and listed at the end. Everything else is reproducible from the excerpts that follow, which embed each builder's decisive function (the veracity mapping, the admission rule, the seeded cluster-disjoint split, the population freeze, the balanced draw, the false-urn draw, the true-feed urn).

subsections.prose: build_fc_gold_selection.py applies Daniel's publisher-admission ruling (a fixed admit list) and keeps only rows dated 2020 or later (claim_date OR review_date), producing fc_gold_v2_admitted.parquet (47,111).

subsections.prose: build_calval_splits.py cuts the CAL/VAL splits from the clustered pool (one row per claim cluster, so the splits are cluster-disjoint by construction). sections.title: 3. Claim extraction
sections.prose: This step reads one outlet post at a time and returns the few self-contained claims a fact-checker would actually check (at most three, often one, none when the post makes no checkable central assertion). It is a single LLM pass, not the older extract/normalize/checkworthy chain. Input is the posts JSON (--posts, with an optional --dates parquet supplying each post's date); output is a JSON file carrying the per-post claims plus a flat claims list that is the input contract for the downstream filter/screen/re-query runs. The production prompt is extract-key-v5, run on DeepSeek-V4-Flash at temperature 0, non-thinking, text-only.

excerpts.caption: The extract-key-v3 base prompt (constant EXTRACT_SYS). Production v5 is this exact text with two extra principles inserted; this block is the byte-identical base.

How the PRODUCTION prompt is built and named: EXTRACT_SYS_V5 = the v3 base with the two _V5_PRINCIPLES paragraphs (prominence/fold + never promote the relayer) spliced in before 'Do not write:'. PROMPT_PRODUCTION = PROMPT_V5, adopted 2026-09-16.

The single model call: one pass per post, temperature 0, max_tokens 4000, JSON object response, non-thinking (reasoning_effort only added when 'gpt-oss' in model). Output is capped at 3 claims each tagged assertion|attribution.

sections.title: 4. Filter and screen
sections.prose: Two further Flash calls run after extraction, each removing or labelling claims. The FILTER rejects malformed or pointless claims; it ships two prompts: filter-key-v1 (retrieval-readiness: is a claim worth searching and well-formed enough to search) which is the CLI default, and filter-survey-v1 (survey-grade: could this be shown to a survey respondent, with a reason code and a fixed-taxonomy subtopic) selected with --prompt. The SCREEN then decides, per kept claim, whether it is US-national-politics/policy in the experiment's form (in_scope) and which side its content favours (lean pro_dem/pro_rep/neutral). Both read the extractor's claims JSON and write per-claim verdict maps; both run DeepSeek-V4-Flash at temperature 0, non-thinking. A claim the model does not rule on is kept (filter) or marked out-of-scope (screen) by default.

excerpts.caption: filter-key-v1 (constant FILTER_SYS): the retrieval-readiness reject predicate — not self-contained, settled by the post itself, not a fact, empty; keep everything else including claims believed true.

filter-survey-v1 (constant FILTER_SURVEY_SYS) plus its SUBTOPICS (14) and REASONS (7) taxonomies: the five survey-grade keep tests, one reason code per claim, and a subject-area label for every claim kept or not.

Filter model call: temperature 0, max_tokens 1500, JSON object, non-thinking. Builds a numbered [i] claim listing; survey mode also parses reason/subtopic; any claim the model omits is kept by default (setdefault keep=True).

screen-key-v1 (constant SCREEN_SYS): SUBJECT (US national politics/policy, with the abroad and crime boundary rules), FORM tests applied to the claim's decisive words, and LEAN (pro_dem/pro_rep/neutral judged on content-if-true).
Screen model call: temperature 0, max_tokens 1500, JSON object, non-thinking. Emits in_scope + domain label + lean per claim; a claim not ruled on defaults to out-of-scope, neutral.

sections.title: 5. Query generation
sections.prose:
For each claim we write exactly one web search query with an LLM (query-v3). The prompt asks for the single load-bearing proposition, at most ten words, aimed at independent reporting rather than commentary. The query block is the resolved claim plus, when available, a neutral one-line context and the claim date. We never fall back to the raw claim text on failure: a raw-claim query is a different query distribution and would contaminate the measurement.

Under --fix an attribution variant (query-v3a) keeps the speaker in the query so that 'X said Y' retrieves whether X said it, not whether Y is true. Off by default; on for the survey mid-band runs.

excerpts.caption: The production query prompt (query-v3), verbatim. One query, ten words, the load-bearing proposition only.
The query-v3a attribution variant (built by string-substitution from query-v3) and the verb-based test that decides when a claim is an attribution claim.
How the query block is assembled (claim + context + date) and the three-try loop that raises rather than ever querying the raw claim text.

sections.title: 6. Retrieval
sections.prose: We send the query to Serper (Google) and keep the top ten results under a date ceiling, with the claim's own origin domain excluded. One search is one request. The date ceiling is the latest date evidence may carry: native claim date, else the extracted utterance date, else review minus one day, and it is hard-clamped to review minus one so the retrieval window can never include the fact-check that produced the gold label. The actual Serper call, scrape and NewsGuard lookup live in src/pipeline/search.py (section on retrieval internals).

excerpts.caption: The Serper call inside run_claim: top ten, origin (and any extra origin) excluded, one request, a single 300s cooldown retry. FC domains are TAGGED not blocked.
The date-ceiling chain and the review-minus-1 hard clamp that makes answer-key leakage structurally impossible.
Expanding a partial extracted date (year, or year-month) to the latest day of its period.
Global request pacing for Serper (50 q/s ceiling).

sections.title: Retrieval internals (search / scrape)
sections.prose: `pipeline/search.py` is the single definition of a web search and a document fetch. `search()` dispatches to a per-provider fetcher (production is Serper), caches on a policy-tagged key, and raises SearchError on API failure so a failed call is never mistaken for 'no evidence'. Serper socials are excluded server-side via priority-ordered `-site:` operators capped at 16 (Google silently drops the excess past its ~32-word budget), then the FULL blocklist is enforced client-side as a guaranteed drop; a small caller exclusion (origin outlet) also goes server-side so Google backfills the slot. `scrape()` fetches + Trafilatura-extracts, strips PDFs via pypdf, and on a miss retries high-value domains once through the Jina Reader paywall fallback; content is judged by no_content() (a length-only test let consent/bot walls through). `newsguard_score_map()` loads the domain->score map used by the credibility rerank.

excerpts.caption: SearchError — an API/HTTP/quota/timeout failure, kept distinct from a genuine 0-results response (which is cached as []).

The server-side social/UGC exclusion machinery: _SOCIAL_PRIORITY ordered by observed leak frequency, _SITE_OP_BUDGET=16 (Google's -site: cap), the blocklist cache tag, and _SERVER_XD_MAX=3 (max caller domains sent server-side). Documents the E1-pilot leak (8.3% of the urn) that motivated the cap.

search(query, top_k, date_ceiling, provider, exclude_domains, min_results): the public entry. Builds the policy-tagged cache key, dispatches to the provider fetcher, caches only on success, tags provenance. date_ceiling = eval-time leakage control (None in production); exclude_domains = the eval-only fact-check block.

The Serper primitives (single source of truth, shared with the async SerperPool): serper_payload (q + -site: excludes + tbs date ceiling + page), serper_headers (X-API-KEY), serper_parse (organic -> result dicts, PDFs kept), serper_finalize (client-side full-blocklist drop), serper_merge (page-2 backfill), _drop_domains, and _fetch_serper (page1 -> optional page2 backfill when the FC block starves min_results).

scrape(url): Trafilatura extraction with cache; PDF text-strip via pypdf; SCRAPE_BLOCKLIST short-circuit; cache-unpin retries (PDF once, Jina once) for stale None/stub entries; high-value-domain Jina Reader paywall fallback; no_content() content-test so a 200 consent/bot wall is not cached as a hit; per-domain rate-limit wait.

sections.title: 7. Evidence filtering rules
sections.prose: Before a document is read, code decides whether it counts and how. Per result we record its NewsGuard tier, a voice key (so mirrored copies of one story are marked), a mirror flag, whether it is a fact-check domain, and a leak flag (published after the ceiling). Which of these turn into a DROP depends on the mode. On every pinned path all --fix hooks are FALSE, so a leaked document is recorded and still read; under --fix drop_leaks, a post-ceiling document is not read and its slot becomes a padded silence. Undated fact-check pages are never read (date-unjudgeable, verdict-bearing). Claim-level exclusions (media/demonstrative hand-read, unresolvable) are RECORDED with a reason, never silently dropped.

excerpts.caption: Per-result bookkeeping: domain, voice key, mirror, NG tier, fc_domain, leak flag, and the region selection feeding the read.
The three code-side skip branches: drop-leaks (only under --fix), undated fact-check page, and empty document. Each becomes a first-class non-observation, not a silent gap.
Parsing Serper's human-format dates to decide if a document postdates the ceiling (unparseable or missing = not a leak).
The claim-level exclusion gate: hand-read media/demonstrative calls and unresolvable claims are recorded with a reason, never silenced.

sections.title: Credibility / domains
sections.prose: Source credibility is a transparent, LLM-free domain prior. `pipeline/config.py` holds the retrieval caps (SEARCH_RETRIEVE_K=10, SEARCH_KEEP_K=5, MAX_ROUNDS=4), the ~33-domain UGC SCRAPE_BLOCKLIST (login/UGC only — newspapers/publishers are NOT blocked), and FACT_CHECK_DOMAINS (excluded from retrieval EVAL-ONLY, to measure independent verification). `pipeline/credibility.py` defines TRUSTED_FACTCHECKERS (IFCN-class, international) and is_primary_source (gov-TLD patterns + IGO/stats/court/legislature allowlist — a single primary read can close a claim). The three helpers `evidence_urn_run` imports from `verify_tweet_claims.py` classify each retrieved doc: _domain_of (URL -> bare domain), _voice_key (collapse to one publisher voice so sisters/subdomains never double-count), _rel_info (PRIMARY / RELIABLE+NG / UNRATED / UNRELIABLE, with fact-checkers and Wikipedia as reliable voices).

excerpts.caption: Tier-3 retrieval caps: MAX_ROUNDS=4, SEARCH_RETRIEVE_K=10 (do-not-raise: the plan ignores num>10), SEARCH_KEEP_K=5 (kept after credibility rerank), REDUNDANCY_THRESHOLD=0.9, the Serper->Exa provider cascade and per-provider round budget.

The UGC-only SCRAPE_BLOCKLIST (~33 domains: social platforms, forums, podcast hosts) — login/UGC walls only; editing it rotates the search cache key by design. Newspapers/paywalled/scientific publishers are deliberately NOT here.

FACT_CHECK_DOMAINS: the ~26-domain fact-checker set excluded from search ONLY in the eval that measures verdict-WITHOUT-reading-a-fact-checker. NOT used in production (where finding a fact-check is the point). Starvation triggers page-2 backfill in _fetch_serper.
TRUSTED_FACTCHECKERS: internationally-extended IFCN-class fact-checkers (a full read from one counts as a STRONG reliable voice, since NewsGuard's map is US-centric) + is_trusted_factchecker().

Primary-source detection: _GOV_SUFFIXES + _GOV_CC regex + PRIMARY_SOURCES allowlist (IGOs, national stats agencies, central banks, courts, legislatures, journals of record) and is_primary_source(). One qualifying primary read can close a claim, so it is deliberately conservative.
_domain_of(url): regex the host out of a URL, strip www., lowercase.

_voice_key(dom): collapse a domain to its editorial voice — publisher-family membership first (e.g. the Sun's four domains), else the registrable base (news.yahoo.com -> yahoo.com) — so subdomains/sisters never count as two independent corroborating voices.

_rel_info(dom, url, scores): the reliability tag for an evidence entry — PRIMARY (gov), RELIABLE (fact-checker=NG_STRONG, or NewsGuard>=60, or Wikipedia=75), UNRATED, or UNRELIABLE (NG<60). Drives the corroboration counting.

sections.title: 8. The reader: prompt, model, parsing
sections.prose:
The reader is the heart of the instrument. One LLM call judges one document against one claim and returns JSON: a direction flag, the sentence numbers it relied on, and a reason (only for I). The model is deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash, temperature 0, response forced to a JSON object, with logprobs on so the flag token's confidence is kept as a soft vote. The document is fed as a numbered sentence list so the evidence pointers reconstruct exactly.

The production reader at this commit is read-v5 (seven flags, READ_SYS_MODE): evidence_urn_run.py sets READ_SYS = READ_SYS_MODE as the default (Daniel 2026-09-21). read-v6.1 (six flags, READ_SYS_V6_1) is the same base rubric with the '3' contested button removed; it is the archived 2026-09-14 experiment, still selectable via --reader read-v6.1. Both are below, verbatim, together with the base rubric and the silver-labeller prompt used to build the doc-level gold. The mode blocks (attribution vs assertion) are defined once in claim_modes.py and imported, but the production read-v5 strips them back out (three successive mode wordings each inverted a stratum; see the file's own comments).

sections.title: 9. From reader output to a document flag
sections.prose: A read returns one of the flags in the DIRECTIONS set. When a document is split into more than one region (rare, K=1 by default) the regions are aggregated deterministically: support-and-refute together becomes '3' with a region-conflict marker, otherwise the strongest flag on the winning side. A document whose reads all failed is marked read_status 'failed' so it is excluded from the claim's evidence count at fit time rather than counted as silence.

sections.title: 10. Weights and the score
sections.prose: Each retrieved document is one voice. The reader emits a flag; each flag carries a fitted log-likelihood-ratio weight w = log( P(flag | claim TRUE) / P(flag | claim FALSE) ), Laplace-smoothed (+1 per flag, +K on each class total). A claim's score is the sum of its documents' flag weights. Every claim is padded to PAD_TO = 10 slots: any slot that returned no read flag (short result list, empty search, dead fetch) counts as a silent document (flag I), so a claim that read nothing stays in as ten silences instead of being dropped. The committed 3-voice urn (fit_urn.fit/score) collapses flags to support / refute / silent; the graded urn (graded_urn.fit_graded/score_graded) keeps one weight per flag — seven (5/4/3/X/I/2/1) or six (--six-flag folds contested 3 into X). Weights are always fitted out-of-fold on the other four of five cluster-disjoint folds. The frozen survey-selection instrument (weights_v5_ceiling_bal3000.json) is exactly this graded fit, read-v5 seven-flag, on the balanced 3,000-claim slice. fit_two_urn is the label-free variant: it never fits on fc-gold, deriving w = log(p_TRUE / p_FALSE) by de-mixing a contaminated timeline urn against a CN-false urn. score_frozen_urn applies pinned ladder weights with no refit.

excerpts.expect: score = n_t * w_t + n_f * w_f + n_empty * w_e

3-voice fit: per-voice log-LR with Laplace +1 / +3, and the score = n_t·w_t + n_f·w_f + n_e·w_e.
The graded flag sets: seven flags (FLAGS7) or six (FLAGS6, contested 3 folded into X by flag_counts).
Graded fit: one Laplace-smoothed (+1 / +K) log-LR per flag; score_graded sums weight×count; oof_graded refits per fold.

The FROZEN survey-selection instrument: read-v5 seven-flag weights, boundary -4.0115, fit on the balanced 3,000-claim ceiling-reads slice (AUC 0.8569, recall@2%FPR 0.4167).
Label-free two-urn fit: w = log(p_TRUE / p_FALSE), with p_TRUE de-mixed from the contaminated timeline urn at rate eps (no gold, no refit).

sections.title: 11. The boundary and headline metrics
sections.prose: A score becomes flag/pass at a boundary threshold: flag when score <= threshold. The threshold is the NESTED operating point — within each outer fold the threshold is picked to maximise recall at FPR <= 2% on the four training folds' inner out-of-fold scores, applied to the held-out fold, and the reported boundary is the mean of the five per-fold thresholds (the same quantity refit_v7qa.rating_cuts calls cut_1). FPR is over TRUE claims (flagging a true post is the error the product cannot afford). AUC is Mann-Whitney (ties half); CIs are a 2,000-rep cluster bootstrap (resample cluster_id, seed 707). RESOLVED 2026-09-21 (Daniel): the frozen read-v5 seven-flag instrument is now THE shipped tool. headline_metrics.json holds the frozen read-v5 seven-flag fit on fc_gold_bal3000 — AUC 0.8569, boundary -4.0115, recall@2%FPR 0.417 — the same numbers as weights_v5_ceiling_bal3000.json, written by fit_ceiling_weights.py --ship. The earlier general six-flag read-v6.1 fit on fc_gold_rep1500 (AUC 0.8512, boundary -3.5839) is archived as headline_metrics_v61_sixflag_2026-09-21.json. One historical regime remains beside them: survey-SCORING (prodregime_metrics.json conditions.S, boundary -6.7949), the Arm-S six-flag read-v6.1 fit that cn_survey_score.py used for the 2026-09-16 survey run before the read-v5 freeze; the live survey scorer is now cn_survey_score_v5.py, reading the frozen weights file directly.

sections.title: 12. Concurrency, caching, retries, cost
sections.prose: Every paid DeepInfra call in this project goes through one concurrency controller and one cached/retried/swept pass. The in-repo copy lives in reader_lab.py (the reader re-read runner); the same design is packaged as the shared deepinfra_runner tool (a SEPARATE repo at ~/dev/tools/deepinfra, not this codebase), which is now THE runner for new DeepInfra work. RateGate holds a target in-flight, cuts x0.8 to a floor only when the trailing-60s 429 'model busy' rate exceeds 5% (min sample 20, so a single 429 never cuts), and recovers +10% every clean 30s up to the ceiling; per request a 429/5xx/transport failure is retried on the SAME request with jittered backoff (1,2,4,8,16,cap30; 6 attempts) before it is marked read-failed, and an end-of-run sweep (up to 2 passes) re-runs read-failed items so no run ends with silently missing reads. Results are cached per item so a rerun is free; the shared runner adds a hard spend cap priced from a list-price table when the provider omits estimated_cost. reader_lab.py also keeps the older AdaptiveGate (AIMD, per-429 cut) as --legacy-gate.

excerpts.caption: RateGate: rate-controlled concurrency limiter (target 160 / ceiling 190 per model / floor 32); reacts only to the windowed 429 RATE, cuts x0.8, recovers +10%; injectable clock for offline unit tests.
Per-request retry: POST through the gate, retry 429 'model busy'/5xx/transport with jittered exponential backoff (1,2,4,8,16,cap30) x6, then raise so the caller marks the read failed for the sweep.

Per-(prompt hash, model, claim, rank) JSON cache: ckey hashes the read identity; work() reuses a cached read unless it is a transport-failure, and writes the fresh read to the cache so a rerun costs $0.
End-of-run sweep: delete every read-failed cache entry (transport-exhausted or malformed body, but not max_tokens runaways) and re-run it, up to 2 sweeps.
Per-minute observation line appended to gate_observations.jsonl (target, in-flight, reads/s, 429 count+rate, p50/p95, failed, cuts) so every run doubles as a concurrency probe.
--preflight: hold 96 in-flight for up to 60s on the first N (cached) units and abort if the 429 rate exceeds 20% before committing the whole run.

reader_lab_score.py: score a re-read against document-level gold (labels_*.json), reporting exact-flag agreement, polarity agreement, and the two polarity inversions that matter (gold-for read as against, gold-against read as for).
Shared tool: RateGate lifted verbatim (same defaults/arithmetic) from reader_lab.py, with an injectable log and the observation writer moved into an Observer class.
Shared tool: append-only per-item JSONL cache, one {key,item_id,result} line per item, last line wins; terminal failures are NOT cached so the sweep and next run retry them.
Shared tool: the same per-request retry (429/5xx/transport, jittered 1,2,4,8,16,cap30 backoff, then raise for the sweep).

sections.title: 13. Validation
sections.prose: Seven validation tests exercise the seven-flag evidence-urn instrument. All metric primitives (AUC by Mann-Whitney over out-of-fold scores, recall@2%FPR, the nested operating point, and the cluster bootstrap CI) live once in fit_urn.py and are imported everywhere else -- nothing re-implements the model. Each subsection below embeds the metric-computation core and says where the resulting number is stored on disk. Two provenance facts are load-bearing: (1) the shipped headline_metrics.json is written by graded_urn.py --ship (SEVEN-flag), not by fit_urn.py, which explicitly refuses to overwrite it because it holds the 3-voice constants; (2) two of the tests the brief lists as validation runs -- the read-v5 seven-flag FREEZE rescore of the survey pool and the stronger-reader same-claims AUC comparison -- are NOT committed scripts, they are clog-documented procedures built from committed primitives (reported explicitly below).

subsections.heading: 13.1 fc_gold 5-fold out-of-fold AUC + nested recall@2%FPR + headline_metrics.json
subsections.prose: The metric core is in fit_urn.py: recall_at_fpr sweeps every operating point and takes the highest recall inside the FPR budget (FPR measured over gold-TRUE claims); nested_threshold is the honest operating point (per outer fold the threshold is picked on the four training folds' inner out-of-fold scores, applied to the held-out fold, pooled); bootstrap runs the cluster bootstrap (resample cluster_id) beside the old class-stratified row bootstrap, 2000 reps seed 707, folds = 5 by blake2b(cluster_id). graded_urn.py is the SHIPPED driver: fit_graded fits one log-LR weight per reader flag, oof_graded produces the 5-fold oof scores, and ship() writes the seven-flag constants (weights keyed 5/4/3/X/I/2/1, nested threshold = mean of the five per-fold thresholds) to headline_metrics.json. fit_urn.py refuses to write that path (it holds the 3-voice fit).

excerpts.caption: recall_at_fpr: highest recall whose FPR (over gold-TRUE claims) stays within budget; returns (recall, fpr, threshold).

nested_threshold: the headline operating point -- per outer fold pick the threshold on the four training folds' inner out-of-fold scores, apply to the held-out fold, pool held-out recall/realised FPR.
boot_idx: one bootstrap draw -- cluster design resamples clusters with replacement (headline); row design resamples within gold class (old).
bootstrap: cluster + row bootstrap side by side on oof AUC and full-fit weights, 95% CIs and the design effect.
fit_graded / oof_graded: one Laplace-smoothed log-LR weight per reader flag (+1 per flag, +7 on totals), 5-fold out-of-fold scoring, mixed claims excluded from the fit.

ship(): write the fitted seven-flag constants to headline_metrics.json (weights per flag, nested threshold = mean of five per-fold thresholds, n/AUC/recall) -- the file every production consumer reads.
Provenance guard: fit_urn.py refuses to write headline_metrics.json because that path holds the SHIPPED seven-flag constants from graded_urn --ship.

sections.title: 14. Survey pool scoring and selection
sections.prose: Two scripts turn per-claim urn flag counts into a rated, selectable survey pool. score_midband.py is the pure-scoring predecessor: it reads the pinned seven-flag weights, sums them into a per-claim log-odds, and cuts each claim into a survey class (1 / 2 / middle / supported). select_midband.py is the canonical/live script: it does everything score_midband does and adds the W=7 variant-A SELECTION floor on top (a refuting flag on a document published more than 7 days before the post is demoted to X), so it is a strict superset. select_midband --no-floor reproduces score_midband exactly, and both write the same schema, so the report reader takes either. The four mid-band rating cuts are PINNED read-v5 constants (DeepSeek-V4-Flash reader, fit cell graded_urn_7flag), not part of the refit file; the weights ARE read from populations/refit_results.json. The floor is a selection filter over the pinned instrument, not a re-fit of it.

excerpts.caption: score_midband header: weights come from the pinned refit cell graded_urn_7flag (read-v5 on DeepSeek-V4-Flash); the four cuts are pinned constants, not in the refit file; a post's rating is the MIN over its kept key claims.

The four pinned read-v5 cut constants (-4.079 / -2.075 / +0.034 / +5.560) and the class-assignment rule rate(): score <= cut_1 -> class 1, <= cut_2 -> class 2, > cut_5 -> supported, else middle (discarded).

Weights W are read from the refit cell graded_urn_7flag; --cuts-from can override the pinned cuts from a refit's rating_cuts block. Each claim is scored with graded_urn.score_graded(r, W) and rated; n_docs = 10 - I recovers the read documents from the pad-to-ten silences.

The score itself: score_graded is the dot product sum(w[k] * n) of each flag's fitted weight against its document count over the active seven-flag set (5,4,3,X,I,2,1). Pad-to-ten enters as extra I (silence) counts upstream.
Post rating = MIN over the post's kept key claims: worst = min by (class rank, score), so the post inherits its most-refuted claim's class and driving claim.

select_midband header: score_midband plus the W=7 variant-A floor and two extra fields; weights are NOT refitted (a selection filter, not an instrument change). --no-floor reproduces score_midband exactly and must give back the 11:58 lean x class table.
Same pinned read-v5 cut constants as score_midband, plus FLOOR_W = 7 (days) and PAD_TO from fit_urn; rate() is identical to score_midband's class-assignment.

Date parsing for the floor: _doc_date reads Serper's absolute date; _rel_date parses relative Serper dates ('1 day ago') against the crawl date (behind --rel-leak, default OFF) since 127 mid-band relative-dated documents all resolve past the post's ceiling.

counts(): the W=7 floor remap. A refuting flag ('1' or '2') on a document dated more than floor_w days before the claim is remapped to X (silenced); the optional relative-date leak drop removes post-ceiling documents as pad silences; pad-to-PAD_TO tops up I.
The switches: --floor-w (default 7), --no-floor (floor_w=None -> reproduces score_midband), --rel-leak with --crawl-date (enables the relative-date leak drop).
Post rollup with the two extra selection fields: same MIN-over-claims worst-claim logic, plus per-post floor_silenced (sum of demoted documents) and an empty audit field for hand review.

Reproduces the pinned survey_scores_2026-09-17_v5.parquet exactly (245 flagged, AUC 0.6230). The older cn_survey_score.py is the six-flag Arm-S scorer (boundary −6.7949).

subsections.heading: 15.6 Smaller mismatches between code and its description
subsections.prose:
- The fit is a per-flag Laplace-smoothed log-likelihood-ratio, not logistic regression. A methods writer should not describe it as a logistic model: the weights are closed-form log-ratios of class-conditional flag rates (+1 per flag smoothing), and the "design matrix" is per-flag document counts.
- graded_urn.py --ship's docstring says seven-flag; the shipped headline_metrics.json is again seven-flag as of 2026-09-21 (the frozen read-v5 fit, written by fit_ceiling_weights.py --ship). The six-flag file it briefly shipped (2026-09-14) is archived as headline_metrics_v61_sixflag_2026-09-21.json.
- extract / filter / screen default their --model to openai/gpt-oss-120b, while the docstrings and production say deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash; the defaults do not run the production model.
- key_claim_filter.py defaults --prompt to filter-key-v1; the survey-grade filter-survey-v1 needs an explicit flag, so the survey chain is not the argparse default.
- key_claim_screen.py has no band-threshold code; "low band" / "mid band" is only input-file naming, not a computed cut.
- fc_gold_rep1500.parquet is an ids-only slice (1,500 x 1) joined back to fc_gold.parquet; the NewsGuard-map helper the brief expected in credibility.py does not exist there (the loader is search.newsguard_score_map).
- The prompt_hash stamped in run records ties a run to exact prompt bytes: read-v5 = 92404a300e14, read-v6.1 = 57d8dbc5df6d, query-v3 = 602caa42bd95. Use these to tell which reader produced a given results file.
